title: What does this return?
examObjective: Applying correct syntax to write DataWeave transformations to coerce, format, order, and filter data
basics: The path in an `update` case can step into Arrays with an index as well as into Objects with a field name: `.items[0].qty` is the `qty` of the first item.
prompt: Read the script. **What does it return?**

given.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ items: [{ qty: 1 }, { qty: 2 }] } update { case .items[0].qty -> 9 }

solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ items: [{ qty: 1 }, { qty: 2 }] } update { case .items[0].qty -> 9 }

explanation.approach: The index selects one element, so only the first item changes. To change every item, map over the Array instead: an update path does not have a wildcard for "all elements".

snippets.label: The answer
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ items: [{ qty: 1 }, { qty: 2 }] } update { case .items[0].qty -> 9 }

snippets.label: Every item
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{ items: [{ qty: 1 }, { qty: 2 }] } update { case i at .items -> i map { qty: 9 } }
snippets.note: Update the Array as a whole.
